page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and tile operations. Memory capacity is configured at 31.0 GB, yielding 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a single 137 GB local NVMe SSD, while no GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng CPU test and Geekbench single-core score, fall within the average range. Single-threaded gzip compression performs in the top 25%, and text processing shows strong performance. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, rank in the bottom 25%. Memory subsystem performance is a notable bottleneck; read-only large block memory bandwidth is poor, falling in the bottom 10%, while small block read and large block write bandwidths remain in the bottom 25%.

This server configuration is suited for workloads requiring moderate memory capacity and local high-speed storage but limited parallel processing power. Appropriate use cases include Redis caching, where it achieves an average of 7.38 million SET operations per second, and light database operations. It can handle small-scale language model inference, processing 135M parameter models at average speeds, though text generation on 7B models drops to a poor 5.04 tokens per second. The primary tradeoff is the low multi-core efficiency and restricted memory bandwidth, making it less suitable for heavy multi-threaded compilation, intensive image processing, or high-throughput static web serving.
